metrics_note: per-child metrics as trainings_get returns them (valid split, as the NAS page labels them): map50, map5095, f1 at f1ConfThresh, recall; latency in ms on the two hardware targets the platform measures, AI1 and T4. The Jetson is not one of them: F5 stays a device measurement.
selection_rule: plan: the frontier child with the highest mAP@50-95 on the valid split

selected_child.evaluation: not run by the platform; started by hand from the model page at 21:01 UTC (eval IrczVmJNDEsBtBRmizoy)

platform_recommended_children.evaluation: run by the platform at 20:30 UTC (eval QPoGPdNc9zPGYfUxkpgG)

recommended_note: the `recommended` flag is the platform's speed/accuracy pick per hardware bucket, flattened; it is the fastest end of the frontier, not the most accurate child (map5095 83.6 against 96.9). It stands in for the plan's 'device-sized candidate' because NAS children carry no size name.
frontier_note: 37 frontier children plus the 4 baselines; the full table with per-child metrics is on the NAS page of the version (app.roboflow.com/jeremy-gracey/fall_detection-johan-jsi2o/nas-runs/1) and in trainings_get; only the rows cited in the results are transcribed here.
